newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative denies gay sex allegations.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative denies gay sex allegations.

text.p: Conservative member of parliament Jerry Hayes on Saturday denied allegations in a tabloid newspaper that he had a 16-month affair with a teenage male researcher in the House of Commons.
"I emphatically deny the story in the News of the World which is without substance or foundation and I am consulting with my solicitors to take action," he said in a statement.

Britain's best-selling Sunday newspaper alleged that Hayes, 43, had cheated on his wife with 18-year-old Paul Stone. It claimed he got the teenager a House of Commons security pass so they could have meetings inside parliament.
Earlier this week Prime Minister John Major sought to place family values at the heart of the Conservative campaign in the leadup to the next general election which must be called by May.

Despite Hayes' denial, the opposition Labour Party moved swiftly to exploit the story with deputy leader John Prescott telling reporters: ""I said a couple of days ago that John Major's new push on family values was bound to end in tears and it has."
